41: B is correct because Amazon AppFlow is a fully managed integration service that transfers data directly between SaaS sources and the Amazon S3 bucket, eliminating the EC2 instances entirely along with the performance bottleneck and the operational overhead of managing and scaling compute. An S3 event notification that publishes to an Amazon SNS topic handles the user notification automatically when the upload completes, replacing the notification logic that previously ran on the instance. This serverless combination improves performance and minimizes operational overhead, unlike options that retain EC2 instances, require custom EventBridge rules per source, or introduce container management.
42: C is correct because a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 provides private connectivity between the EC2 instances and S3 over the AWS backbone network, so S3 traffic never traverses the NAT gateway and the company avoids NAT gateway data processing charges and cross-Availability Zone data transfer charges. Gateway endpoints cost nothing to create and serve instances in every subnet across all Availability Zones in the VPC, whereas a NAT gateway in one AZ incurs charges for traffic from other AZs. The other options do not eliminate these data transfer charges or add management complexity.
43: B is correct because AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection between the on-premises environment and AWS, so the large, time-sensitive S3 backups no longer compete with internal users for the company's shared internet bandwidth. This gives timely, consistent throughput for backups over the long term while leaving internet connectivity unaffected for internal users. A VPN still traverses the limited internet connection, and daily Snowball transfers cannot deliver time-sensitive ongoing backups.
44: A is correct because enabling versioning on the S3 bucket preserves all object versions, so if critical data is accidentally deleted, the previous version can be immediately restored. B is correct because MFA Delete requires multi-factor authentication to permanently delete an object version or to disable versioning, which prevents even privileged and root users from accidentally destroying the data. Together these two bucket-level features provide protection specifically against accidental deletion.
45: B is correct because subscribing an Amazon SQS queue to the Amazon SNS topic implements the fan-out pattern, so every notification about a new data delivery is durably persisted in the queue even when downstream processing fails due to network connectivity issues. E is correct because modifying the Lambda function to read from the SQS queue means that if the function fails, the message remains in the queue and is automatically retried until it is processed successfully, eliminating the need to manually rerun the job. This combination decouples notification from processing and guarantees that all data is eventually ingested.
46: B is correct because Amazon Macie is a fully managed data discovery service that uses machine learning to automatically detect personally identifiable information in objects stored in S3, which requires virtually no development effort compared with writing custom scanning algorithms. When Macie identifies PII in objects uploaded through the S3 transfer point, its findings can trigger an Amazon SNS notification to alert the administrators so they can remove the offending objects. Options requiring custom Lambda scanning algorithms demand significant development, and Amazon Inspector is a vulnerability scanner that does not detect PII.
47: D is correct because an On-Demand Capacity Reservation reserves EC2 compute capacity in specific Availability Zones for any duration, guaranteeing the company capacity in the three needed AZs for the one-week event while paying standard On-Demand rates. Reserved Instances primarily provide a billing discount and do not guarantee capacity availability in specific Availability Zones on demand. The other options either specify only the Region or use a purchase model that does not assure capacity.
48: D is correct because Amazon EFS is a fully managed, highly available, and durable NFS file system that is accessible concurrently from EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones, so the catalog survives instance failure and is stored redundantly. An EC2 instance store is ephemeral storage that is lost when the instance stops or fails, so the current design is neither highly available nor durable. ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory cache rather than durable storage, and S3 Glacier Deep Archive retrieval takes hours, which is unsuitable for an active catalog.
49: B is correct because S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage patterns, so files accessed randomly within the first year are retrieved quickly and at optimized cost without retrieval fees. An S3 Lifecycle policy then transitions files to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 1 year, where the slower retrieval is acceptable for the infrequently accessed archives. Amazon Athena queries and retrieves the files still in Amazon S3, and S3 Glacier Select queries the archived files.
50: D is correct because AWS Systems Manager Run Command lets a solutions architect execute a custom command that applies the third-party software patch to all 1,000 instances simultaneously and immediately, which remediate the critical vulnerability as quickly as possible. Run Command requires no additional infrastructure beyond the SSM Agent already installed on the instances and executes on demand rather than on a schedule. Patch Manager and maintenance windows are oriented toward scheduled operating system patching baselines and would add configuration overhead and delay for third-party software.
51: B is correct because Amazon SES provides email templates that can format the extracted shipping statistics into an easy-to-read HTML report and send it to multiple email addresses at once. D is correct because an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event can invoke an AWS Lambda function at the same time every morning, and the Lambda function queries the application's REST API, extracts the shipping statistics, and passes the data to SES for formatting and delivery. This serverless combination fully satisfies the scheduling, extraction, formatting, and email requirements.
52: C is correct because Amazon EFS is a fully managed, highly available NFS file system that presents a standard file system structure, scales automatically as data grows, and is accessible from EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Running the application in a Multi-AZ Auto Scaling group ensures the compute tier scales automatically and survives the loss of an Availability Zone with minimal operational overhead. EBS volumes are confined to a single Availability Zone and attached to a single instance, so they cannot deliver the same availability and automatic scaling.
53: C is correct because S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents any user, including administrative and root users, from deleting or overwriting object versions until the 10-year retention period expires, satisfying the immutability requirement. An S3 Lifecycle policy transitioning the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year provides immediate accessibility for the first year and low-cost archival for the remaining 9 years. Both S3 Standard and S3 Glacier Deep Archive replicate data across multiple Availability Zones for maximum resiliency.
54: C is correct because Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is a fully managed native Windows file system that provides SMB file shares, so users can continue accessing files exactly as they do today with existing Windows tooling and Active Directory integration. A Multi-AZ configuration provides automatic failover to a standby in another Availability Zone for high availability, and the managed service replicates data for durability, eliminating the need to synchronize duplicate copies across two EC2 instances. Amazon EFS uses NFS, which is not the native protocol for Windows file shares.
55: C is correct because security groups are stateful and support referencing other security groups, so attaching a security group to the RDS DB instances that allows inbound traffic only from the security group assigned to the EC2 instances in the private subnets enforces the requirement precisely at the instance level. Because the DB instances run in the dedicated database subnets, this security group reference ensures only private-subnet instances can reach them. Route tables and network ACLs operate on CIDR blocks and cannot provide this targeted, allow-only enforcement for a specific set of instances.
56: C is correct because a Regional API Gateway endpoint can be associated with the company's custom domain name, and the public ACM certificate must be imported into the same Region as the Regional endpoint so it can be attached, enabling HTTPS for the third-party services. Configuring Route 53 to route traffic to the API Gateway endpoint points the company's registered domain at the API. ACM certificates for Regional custom domain names must reside in the API's Region, not us-east-1, which makes the other options invalid.
57: B is correct because Amazon Rekognition is a fully managed image moderation API that detects inappropriate content such as explicit or suggestive images with simple API calls, which minimizes development effort. Adding human review for low-confidence predictions, such as through Amazon A2I, provides a safeguard for accurate moderation of user-uploaded images. The other options either address text analysis rather than images or require significant custom machine learning development.
58: C is correct because AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers, so with Amazon ECS on Fargate the company only specifies CPU and memory per task and AWS provisions, scales, and manages the underlying infrastructure entirely. This lets the company focus on maintaining its critical applications while still achieving the required scalability and availability through ECS orchestration. The other options all require the company to provision, patch, and manage EC2 instances.
59: D is correct because Amazon Kinesis Data Streams can capture large volumes of clickstream data in real time from hundreds of global websites and easily scales to handle more than 30 TB per day. Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose then reliably and automatically transmits that data to an Amazon S3 data lake without any infrastructure to manage, and Amazon Redshift provides the large-scale analytics needed on the stored data. This fully managed pipeline scales to the daily volume and eliminates the operational burden of self-managed clusters or EC2 fleets.
60: C is correct because an Application Load Balancer supports a listener rule on the HTTP listener that redirects requests to the HTTPS listener, returning an HTTP 301 response that instructs the client to resend the request over HTTPS. This is the standard ALB mechanism to force all traffic to HTTPS without changing the client or the backend application. Network ACLs cannot perform redirects, and replacing the ALB would remove the Layer 7 capabilities needed for the redirect.
